The improvements in survival of gynaecological cancer in the Anglia region of England appear to be primarily attributed to the centralization of care and the implementation of multidisciplinary management, as evident from the provided healthcare Q&A matches.

These improvements are observed in several match summaries:

* The adoption of 1999 guidance on gynaecological cancer, which included multidisciplinary case management and centralisation of surgery, resulted in a marked step-change improvement in survival of gynaecological cancer in an area of eastern England in 2000.
* A multidisciplinary clinic has been reported to have provided the first report demonstrating benefits described above, highlighting its potential as a effective model for improving care.

While other factors such as lifestyle and socioeconomic status may also play roles, the centralization of care and implementation of multidisciplinary management are identified as key contributing factors to these improvements.
